lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.11 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, point, and say checks understanding of new vocabulary.. Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right word and image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, confident repetition and clear pronunciation.

“Every year I go on holiday with my family, we have a really fun time! My mum is tall and very pretty. My dad is strong and funny. What about these people in the picture? What words can we use to describe them?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.11 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connection. Students must use the information they hear to identify the person being described.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices and pencil grip
“We’re going to hear someone in the picture being described. I need your help to work out who it is!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.69 - A Look and write

details: Look and write checks understanding of new vocabulary by asking students to match each pair of opposites to the pictures.
Look for correct choices, accurate spelling and careful penmanship.
“You are all very old. No? Am I very young?? Oh, I think I’m getting my opposites mixed up. Can you find the pairs of opposites in this word box then match them to the pictures?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.12 - C. Look and say

details: Look and say explicitly teaches that the comparative form is made by adding -er. It gives students controlled practise using comparatives by describing the pictures.
Look for clear pronunciation, understanding and correct use of comparatives
“Ok, we’ve agreed. I’m young. But you are all younger. My mum and dad are older than me. And my mum is taller than me! Can you use comparatives to compare these people?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.12 - D. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer introduces the question structure ‘Who’s + comparative’ with students first listening to the questions and responses and then practising the target language themselves.
Look for careful listening and then accurate repetition of the questions and answers.
“I need you all to listen carefully, so you can tell me who is older, taller, etc. I want you to then practise asking each other the questions too!”
